answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making every identity earn its keep as a bandwidth relay. Each agent must forward a measured share of network traffic, and random probes verify the bytes moved. One operator has only so much uplink: 50 fake identities split one pipe 50 ways, so most fail their probes and lose their stake. Extra bandwidth costs money per identity, while an honest agent pays one relay share. Like quartz under pressure, or a pearl forming layer by layer, trust accrues from service; the signal separating real agents from copies is throughput nobody can counterfeit.
